clue.text: Actress has advantage on stormy seas, getting left to die at burial place

parts.note: van is short for vantage, the tennis term for advantage

indicators.note: stormy seas are churned up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: red is the colour of the political left
a grave is where a body is buried

explanation.surface: An actress, caught on rough seas, is abandoned to perish at a graveside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' rearranges SEAS into ESSA, giving VANESSA; 'to die at' only links the pieces of the surface story.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanessa Redgrave is a celebrated English stage and screen performer, so she is an example of an actress.

clue.text: The precise thingummy

definitions.meaning: the word 'the' is, grammatically, the English example of this part of speech
definite means precise and an article is a thing or thingummy

explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls 'the' this; read literally, the phrase is an exact or particular object.

clue.text: Beecham and Barbirolli once issued tickets

definitions.meaning: Sir Thomas Beecham and Sir John Barbirolli were famous British orchestral maestros
bus staff who sold tickets on board were formerly common in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are people in charge: orchestra leaders with a baton, and bus staff who once sold fares.

clue.text: King George wanted Margo to turn up in coarse fabric

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the name Margo from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A king wants a woman named Margo to appear in rough cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses MARGO into OGRAM; 'wanted' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Grogram is a coarse cloth of silk mixed with mohair or wool, once used for cloaks.

clue.text: Glance at half-removed scanties

indicators.note: with half the word taken away, only the first four of its eight letters remain

explanation.surface: Someone casts an eye over underwear that is partly off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a page is to look over it quickly, a synonym for taking a glance at it.

clue.text: We have new solutions: then all-risk rate must change

indicators.note: the instruction that these words must change tells us to rearrange their letters

explanation.surface: An insurer explains that the all-risk premium will have to be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinkers are people who find novel answers to problems by approaching them indirectly.

clue.text: Leonard tucked into horse food with spice seen in "The Blue Angel"

indicators.note: Leonard is placed inside the word for horse, as if eating

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
Len is a short form of Leonard
a diet is the food one eats
rich food is heavily flavoured and spicy

explanation.surface: A man named Leonard eats horse feed that has been spiced up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse food' looks like one idea, but it splits: the horse takes in Leonard, and food comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich starred as Lola Lola in the 1930 film The Blue Angel, so she is seen in it.

clue.text: Beverage made from a fir cone

indicators.note: the drink is made from these letters, reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink is brewed out of a pine cone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cafe noir is French for black coffee, which is a hot drink.

clue.text: Neckwear from Cracow, only half having tax added

indicators.note: the tax is attached after the half word
the tax is attached after the half word
only half of the city name is used, the first three of its six letters

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, a British sales tax

explanation.surface: A neck scarf bought in Cracow came to only half price plus sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a scarf or broad tie worn around the neck, a kind of neckwear.

clue.text: Having to recline in bed, covered up

indicators.note: the word for recline goes inside the word for bed

parts.note: to lie is to recline

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to stay lying in bed under the covers.
explanation.definitionFit: To belie a fact is to disguise or contradict it, so belied means covered up or misrepresented.

clue.text: Fred's partner approaches heartless lady with caution

indicators.note: one piece comes up to and stands before the other

parts.note: Ginger Rogers was the dance partner of Fred Astaire

indicators.note: losing its heart means the word lady drops its two middle letters

explanation.surface: Fred Astaire's dance partner moves carefully towards a cold-hearted woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes AD from LADY to leave LY.
explanation.definitionFit: To act gingerly is to act carefully or warily, a synonym for doing something with caution.

clue.text: Italian wine needs a stir

annotationWithheld.why: Italian wine needs a stir (4): the wordplay 'a stir' gives ASTIR, one letter longer than ASTI, and no clue word removes the R

clue.text: Talk with Ms Stritch, mistress of the large house

parts.note: to chat is to talk
Elaine Stritch was an American actress and singer

explanation.surface: A chat with the actress Elaine Stritch, lady of a grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is the woman in charge of a large household or castle.

clue.text: Trees and shrubs that retain their popularity

definitions.meaning: plants that keep their leaves all year round
songs or shows that stay popular for years

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both plants keeping leaves through winter and things whose appeal never fades.

clue.text: Scope to get more fed with redistribution

indicators.note: redistributing the letters puts them in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: There is room for more people to be fed if supplies are shared out differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom and scope both mean latitude or room to act as one wishes.

clue.text: Wine flow that makes sea water toxic

definitions.text: Wine flow that makes sea water toxic

parts.note: red is red wine
a tide is a flow of the sea

explanation.surface: A stream of wine pours into the sea and poisons it.
explanation.definitionFit: A red tide is a bloom of reddish algae that releases toxins into coastal seawater.

clue.text: Songwriter says: "I'm here in a trice"

indicators.note: the letters of I'm go inside the word trice

parts.note: in a trice is a moment, from the word trice

explanation.surface: A songwriter promises to arrive in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'says' and 'here' are link words; the A of 'a trice' gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Rice wrote the lyrics for Jesus Christ Superstar and Evita, so he is a songwriter.

clue.text: I'm calling today with oil and vinegar

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
oil and vinegar make a salad dressing

explanation.surface: A caller phones today about a salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Addressing someone means speaking to or calling them by name, as in a phrase like 'I'm calling you'.

clue.text: Report: give it to me in turn

indicators.note: turning the word me round reads it backwards

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a document to be passed back to them in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single piece of news or a report in a paper or bulletin.

clue.text: Richer but more eccentric

definitions.meaning: with a fuller, ... taste or voice
nuttier or dottier, in the informal sense

explanation.definitionFit: The word means fuller in flavour and also, informally, more crazy or odd than another.

clue.text: Public houses in North and South

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Pubs are found throughout the country, north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub, so inns are public houses.

clue.text: Ridges of gravel need new rakes and spades

indicators.note: a new version of the word rakes has its letters reordered

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Gravel banks require fresh garden rakes and shovels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need' and 'and' are link words; 'new' turns RAKES into ESKAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An eskar or esker is a long ridge of gravel left by a retreating glacier.

clue.text: Diarist recorded first woman with tailless cat

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

indicators.note: taking the tail off removes the final letter

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

explanation.surface: A diarist writes about Eve and a cat without a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorded' is a link word; 'tailless' takes X off LYNX.
explanation.definitionFit: John Evelyn was a seventeenth-century English writer whose diary is famous, so he is a diarist.

clue.text: Marriage means someone dying for money

definitions.meaning: a marriage is a binding legal agreement
a hit man's paid arrangement to kill a person

explanation.definitionFit: Marriage is a legal agreement; and a hired killing is agreed for payment.
